title: Screen-Time vs Mood Trade-off
dataSources: Mood entries (`mood:entry`), meditation sessions (`meditation:session`), journal entries (`journal:entry`), gratitude logs (`gratitude:log`).
app: Mood, mindfulness and journaling apps — Daylio / How We Feel mood exports, Headspace / Insight Timer meditation logs, journaling and gratitude entries — sent to Splunk HEC via scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal (sourcetype=mood:entry OR sourcetype=screentime:usage)
| bin _time span=1d
| stats avg(mood_score) as mood, sum(minutes) as screen by _time
| eval heavy=if(screen>240,"heavy screen","lighter")
| stats avg(mood) as avg_mood by heavy
description: Compares your mood on heavy-screen days versus lighter ones, testing whether more scrolling really means feeling worse.
value: Seeing your own mood dip on high-screen days is far more motivating than generic warnings about screen time.
implementation: Join mood with screen-time in `index=personal`; compare average mood by screen load.
visualization: Bar chart of average mood on heavy versus light screen days.
grandmaExplanation: It compares your mood on days of heavy phone use versus lighter days, testing whether scrolling brings you down.
